narrative: The only net contraction in the series: active codes fell by 1,970 (853,835 → 851,865) as removals (5,620) outran additions (3,650) for the only time across six snapshots.

Removals were broad — Ontario (1,792), Quebec (1,030), Alberta (980) and New Brunswick (846) — the look of a consolidation pass retiring low-volume or duplicate rural routes rather than any single event.

The cycle's standout is New Brunswick: 15,640 of the 17,185 CSD reassignments are there. This is the postal-code footprint of New Brunswick's 2023 local-governance reform, which merged some 340 local entities into 90 — the municipality field catching up to the province's redrawn map.

Real city renames are few (359) and rural-Alberta flavoured — codes shuffling between Spruce Grove and Parkland County, Drayton Valley and Brazeau County — the ongoing town-versus-county boundary churn that recurs in every Prairie release.

removed: The sole net contraction. Spread evenly across the big provinces with no dominant region, it reads as routine retirement of stale routes rather than a structural change.
csd_changed: New Brunswick's 15,640 reassignments map onto its 2023 local-governance reform (roughly 340 entities merged into 90). The physical addresses didn't move; their municipal identifiers were rewritten to the new structure.
